questions.question: Studies show that nearly ______ of motorcycle riders killed in crashes had been drinking.

options.text: 20 percent
40 percent
60 percent
80 percent

questions.correctAnswerText: 40 percent
questions.explanation: Alcohol causes many motorcycle crashes, especially fatal ones. Research shows that about 40 percent of motorcycle riders killed in crashes had been drinking.

questions.question: If a small animal enters your lane while you are riding in traffic, you should:

options.text: Do whatever you can, including swerving into other lanes, to avoid hitting the animal.
Switch lanes as quickly as possible.
Stay in your lane.
Flash your lights to scare the animal away.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay in your lane.
questions.explanation: Try to avoid hitting an animal safely. However, if you are in traffic, stay in your lane. Swerving into another lane can cause you to crash into another vehicle. Hitting a small animal is safer than hitting another car.

questions.question: A linked braking system:

options.text: Connects the front and rear brakes so both brakes apply when you use either brake lever.
Connects the front brake to the gear shifter so the brake applies when you downshift.
Connects the rear brake to a foot control.
Connects the rear brake to a switch on the handlebar.

questions.correctAnswerText: Connects the front and rear brakes so both brakes apply when you use either brake lever.
questions.explanation: A linked braking system connects the front and rear brakes on a motorcycle. When you use either brake lever, both brakes get braking power. Check your owner's manual to learn about your motorcycle's braking system.

questions.question: Because motorcycles are small, they may seem to be:

options.text: Traveling faster than they actually are.
Traveling more slowly than they actually are.
Not moving when they actually are.
Closer than they actually are.

questions.correctAnswerText: Traveling faster than they actually are.
questions.explanation: Because of their small size, motorcycles may look like they are going faster than they really are.

questions.question: When riding in a group, where should inexperienced riders position themselves?

options.text: Just behind the leader.
In front of the group.
At the rear of the group.
Beside the leader.

questions.correctAnswerText: Just behind the leader.
questions.explanation: Inexperienced riders should ride near the front of the group, right behind the leader. This way, more experienced riders behind them can watch and help them.

questions.question: How much of a motorcycle's stopping power comes from the front brake?

options.text: About 25 percent
About 50 percent
About 70 percent
100 percent

questions.correctAnswerText: About 70 percent
questions.explanation: The front brake is more powerful than the rear brake. It provides about 70 percent of your motorcycle's total stopping power.

questions.question: What does this hand signal mean?

options.text: Slow or stop
Left turn
Right turn
Backing up

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow or stop
questions.explanation: Riders can use hand signals instead of or along with turn signals. When a rider bends their left arm at the elbow and points it downward, it means they are slowing down or stopping.

questions.question: On a slippery surface, what should you NOT do?

options.text: Reduce your speed.
Avoid making sudden moves.
Use only the front brake when slowing or stopping.
Use both brakes when slowing or stopping.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use only the front brake when slowing or stopping.
questions.explanation: To ride safely on a slippery surface, use both brakes when slowing or stopping, reduce your speed, and avoid sudden moves. Watch for oily areas, dirt, gravel, shaded areas, and bridges—these are more slippery.

questions.question: If you must brake and swerve to avoid a hazard, you should:

options.text: Do one action, then the other.
Do both actions at the same time.
Always brake first, then swerve.
Try to use only the brakes instead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do one action, then the other.
questions.explanation: If you need to brake and swerve, do them one at a time. Brake then swerve, or swerve then brake. Never do both at the same time.

questions.question: Which vest or jacket color helps you be seen best?

options.text: Red
Black
Silver
Blue

questions.correctAnswerText: Red
questions.explanation: Wear bright clothing when riding to be more visible. Bright orange, yellow, red, or green are best. Avoid dark or dull colors.

questions.question: In hot weather, wearing a riding jacket:

options.text: Helps protect against heat exhaustion and dehydration.
Is not recommended because it can cause heat-related problems.
Should only be worn if the jacket is light colored.
Is not important.

questions.correctAnswerText: Helps protect against heat exhaustion and dehydration.
questions.explanation: Wear a riding jacket and long pants in hot weather. They protect you from injuries and also help prevent heat exhaustion and dehydration.

questions.question: Should you wear a leather jacket while riding in warm weather?

options.text: No, it will make you too hot.
Yes, but take frequent breaks to remove the jacket and cool off.
Yes, riding jackets are designed to keep you cool, even in warm weather.
No, jackets get in the way of steering.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yes, riding jackets are designed to keep you cool, even in warm weather.
questions.explanation: In warm weather, a riding jacket helps prevent dehydration and protects you from injury. Many jackets are designed to protect riders from overheating, even in warm weather.

questions.question: When riding in a group, riders should:

options.text: Spread out to make the group easier to see.
Stay close together to make the group easier to see.
Separate occasionally.
Ride in pairs.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay close together to make the group easier to see.
questions.explanation: When riding in a group, stay close together but allow enough space around each rider. This makes the group easier for others to see and keeps riders from getting separated. Do not pair up because it does not leave enough room to move.

questions.question: A rider can discourage other vehicles from sharing their lane by:

options.text: Riding in the left portion of the lane.
Riding in the center portion of the lane.
Giving dirty looks if another driver moves into the lane.
Riding in a zigzag pattern to fill up the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Riding in the center portion of the lane.
questions.explanation: Ride in the center of your lane to discourage other drivers from trying to squeeze in beside you.

questions.question: A helmeted rider is _______ more likely to survive a crash than a rider without a helmet.

options.text: Two times
Three times
Six times
20 times

questions.correctAnswerText: Three times
questions.explanation: Riders without helmets are three times more likely to die from head injuries in a crash than riders wearing helmets.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Plans to turn left.
Is about to stop.
Plans to turn right.
Is about to slow down.

questions.correctAnswerText: Plans to turn right.
questions.explanation: Instead of turn signals, riders can use hand signals. If a rider's left arm is bent at the elbow and pointing upward, it means the rider plans to turn right or change lanes to the right.

questions.question: When turning a motorcycle, you should:

options.text: Press the grip in the direction you want to turn.
Press the grip opposite to the direction you want to turn.
Not hold the grip because it can be dangerous.
Not lean the motorcycle because it is unsafe.

questions.correctAnswerText: Press the grip in the direction you want to turn.
questions.explanation: At speeds faster than a walk, your motorcycle needs to lean to turn. Press the grip in the direction you want to turn, and the motorcycle will lean the right way.

questions.question: When planning a long group ride, which idea should NOT be used?

options.text: Plan travel distances based on the least experienced rider.
Skip breaks so riders can reach their destination faster.
Put less experienced riders behind the leaders.
Use a staggered riding formation.

questions.correctAnswerText: Skip breaks so riders can reach their destination faster.
questions.explanation: Base route length on the least experienced rider's abilities. Take regular breaks to reduce fatigue. Place less experienced riders behind the leader so more experienced riders can watch them. Ride in a staggered formation.

questions.question: Maximum straight-line braking is done by:

options.text: Using the front brake first, then the rear brake.
Using the rear brake first, then the front brake.
Using both brakes at the same time without locking either wheel.
Using both brakes at the same time and locking the rear wheel.

questions.correctAnswerText: Using both brakes at the same time without locking either wheel.
questions.explanation: Maximum braking happens when you apply both brakes at the same time without locking either wheel.

questions.question: A passenger on a motorcycle should:

options.text: Get on before the engine starts.
Get on after the engine starts.
Sit as far back as possible on the motorcycle.
Hold onto the seat.

questions.correctAnswerText: Get on after the engine starts.
questions.explanation: Passengers should get on only after the engine has started and the transmission is in neutral. Sit as far forward as possible without blocking the rider's control and hold onto the rider's waist, hips, or belt.

questions.question: When riding in rain or fog, you should:

options.text: Use your high beam headlight.
Use your low beam headlight.
Not use your headlight.
Switch between low and high beam headlights.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use your low beam headlight.
questions.explanation: Use your low beam headlight in rain, snow, or fog. High beams reflect off these conditions and make it harder to see.

questions.question: A rectangular sign is usually a:

options.text: School crossing sign.
Railroad crossing sign.
Stop sign.
Speed limit sign.

questions.correctAnswerText: Speed limit sign.
questions.explanation: Rectangular signs are white with black letters or symbols. They show road rules like speed limits. You must follow all rules on these signs.

questions.question: When braking, you should:

options.text: Apply the front brake first, then the rear.
Apply the rear brake first, then the front.
Use both brakes at the same time.
Use brakes in any order.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use both brakes at the same time.
questions.explanation: Always use both brakes together when you slow down or stop.

questions.question: When choosing a helmet, all of these are important except:

options.text: The helmet meets DOT standards.
The helmet looks nice.
The helmet fits snugly.
The helmet has no damage.

questions.correctAnswerText: The helmet looks nice.
questions.explanation: Choose a helmet that meets DOT standards. It must fit snugly and have no cracks, loose padding, or frayed straps. Appearance does not affect safety.

questions.question: On a three-wheeled motorcycle or with a sidecar, do not ride too far to the right because:

options.text: Other drivers may not see you.
You will not be able to pass other vehicles easily.
Other drivers may try to share your lane.
You may run off the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may run off the road.
questions.explanation: A sidecar extends to the right, and the right wheel on a three-wheeled motorcycle can go off the road if you ride too far right. Stay in the center of your lane.
